name: dia
description: Thirteen reasoning-and-review skills, each a function with one purpose, and dia, the one skill that calls them: dia-skopos shows what is asked and the result it is for before work, dia-techne does a task for the outcome it serves and has it checked outside the model, dia-emend reviews a draft once, dia-ratchet revises in rounds that move only on outside evidence, dia-regula writes or reviews text a model follows by four rules, dia-negative holds a claim to its own standard, dia-reductio holds a position against its own commitments, dia-warrant tests the step that carries a conclusion, dia-conjecture tests a claim about every case by counterexamples, dia-counterplan builds the plan the opposite assumptions give, dia-adjudicate rules on reports about a target by the evidence, and dia-elenchus and dia-quaestio question an idea in a dialogue. A skill starts only when its name starts the message; dia with a target has it criticised by three independent agents and judged by a fourth.
